Nigeria Micro-nutrient Deficiencies

Introduction

Nigeria micro-nutrient deficiency data sources

There are number of sources of food consumption and micro-nutrient deficiency data. The three main sources identified for Nigeria have different dates, and differing number of deficiencies and populations ( Table 1 ).

(Federal Government of Nigeria (FGoN) and International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) 2024) (Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria (FMoHSW) et al. 2025) (Ishida et al. 2026 (submitted))

The data at state level need to be joined to the Nigeria States spatial dataset, and the data at zone level need to be joined to the geopolitical zones.

The stages are:

  1. Load the States dataset
  2. Load the geopolitical zone
  3. Load each health database
  4. For each indicator in the database join to the state or zone spatial dataset and plot

Load the States

The source of the states data is from OSGOF-Ehealth-UNCS. These have previously been cleaned to remove sliver polygons and gaps, and were saved as a topojson format.

Show the code 
vect_state_geo <- vect("D:/DatosProyecto/SpatialData/Africa/Pais/Nigeria/NGA Admin 2019-2025 OSGOF-Ehealth-UNCS/nga_admin1_topo.topojson")

crs(vect_state_geo) <- "epsg:4326"

vect_state_geo$adm1_pcode <- as.factor(vect_state_geo$adm1_pcode)

# levels(vect_state_geo$adm1_pcode) # Check levels

ggplot(vect_state_geo)+
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = adm1_pcode)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = adm1_pcode), size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Nigeria States",
    fill = "State<br>Code") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

Show the code 
df_state <- as.data.frame(vect_state_geo)

Load the geopolitical zones

The geopolitical zones are a combination of states with similar ethnic groups, and/or common political history.

There are six zones:

Zone name States
North Central Benue, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Niger, and Plateau States, and Federal Capital Territory
North East Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, and Yobe
North West Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara
South East Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo
South South Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo, and Rivers
South West Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, and Oyo

The zones are created by joining the states.

Show the code 
adm1_pcode <- c("NG001", "NG002", "NG003", "NG004", "NG005", "NG006",
"NG007", "NG008", "NG009", "NG010", "NG011", "NG012", "NG013", "NG014",
"NG015", "NG016", "NG017", "NG018", "NG019", "NG020", "NG021", "NG022",
"NG023", "NG024", "NG025", "NG026", "NG027", "NG028", "NG029", "NG030",
"NG031", "NG032", "NG033", "NG034", "NG035", "NG036", "NG037")

geopolitical_zone <- c("South East", "North East", "South South", 
"South East", "North East", "South South", "North Central", "North East",
"South South", "South South", "South East", "South South", "South West",
"South East", "North Central", "North East", "South East", "North West",
"North West", "North West", "North West", "North West", "North Central",
"North Central", "South West", "North Central", "North Central", 
"South West", "South West", "South West", "South West", "North Central", 
"South South", "North West", "North East", "North East", "North West")

df_gpz <- tibble(adm1_pcode, geopolitical_zone)

vect_gpz_geo <- dplyr::left_join(vect_state_geo, df_gpz, by =
c("adm1_pcode")) |> aggregate(by = "geopolitical_zone")

ggplot(vect_gpz_geo)+
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = geopolitical_zone)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = geopolitical_zone), size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Nigeria Geopolitical Zones",
    fill = "Zone<br>Name") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

NFCMS 2021

Load the database

The NFCMS data are loaded and there are data available for the following zones:

Show the code 
df_NFCMS <- read.csv("E:/repos/Biofort_Atlas_Nigeria/tab_data/NFCMS_deficiencies.csv")

df_NFCMS$geopolitical_zone <- as.factor(df_NFCMS$geopolitical_zone) 

cat(paste(levels(df_NFCMS$geopolitical_zone), "; ")) # Check levels

North Central ; North East ; North West ; South East ; South South ; South West ;

Join the NFCMS database to the zone dataset

The NFCMS dataset does not contain codes for the zones - only names. Therefore we need to join the two data frames using the name of the zone - and checking that all zones have data.

Show the code 
vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS <- dplyr::left_join(vect_gpz_geo, df_NFCMS, by = c("geopolitical_zone"))
vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS |> as.data.frame() |> 
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = F,
    filter = "bottom",
    selection = list(mode = "none"),
    editable = FALSE,
    options = list(
      digits = 0,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      scrollCollapse = TRUE,
      autoWidth = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = list(leftColumns = 2),
      lengthMenu = c(15, 40),
      pageLength = 15
    ))

NDHS 2023-24

Load the databases

The NDHS state data are loaded and there are data available for the following states:

Show the code 
df_NDHS_state <- read.csv("E:/repos/Biofort_Atlas_Nigeria/tab_data/NDHS_state_deficiencies.csv")
# change name to match states dataset
df_NDHS_state['State'][df_NDHS_state['State'] == "FCT-Abuja"] <- "Federal Capital Territory"

df_NDHS_state$State <- as.factor(df_NDHS_state$State) 

cat(paste(levels(df_NDHS_state$State), "; ")) # Check levels

Abia ; Adamawa ; Akwa Ibom ; Anambra ; Bauchi ; Bayelsa ; Benue ; Borno ; Cross River ; Delta ; Ebonyi ; Edo ; Ekiti ; Enugu ; Federal Capital Territory ; Gombe ; Imo ; Jigawa ; Kaduna ; Kano ; Katsina ; Kebbi ; Kogi ; Kwara ; Lagos ; Nasarawa ; Niger ; Ogun ; Ondo ; Osun ; Oyo ; Plateau ; Rivers ; Sokoto ; Taraba ; Yobe ; Zamfara ;

The NDHS zone data are loaded and there are data available for the following zones:

Show the code 
df_NDHS_zone <- read.csv("E:/repos/Biofort_Atlas_Nigeria/tab_data/NDHS_zone_deficiencies.csv")

df_NDHS_zone$Zone <- as.factor(df_NDHS_zone$Zone) 

cat(paste(levels(df_NDHS_zone$Zone), "; ")) # Check levels

North Central ; North East ; North West ; South East ; South South ; South West ;

Join the NDHS database to the state dataset

The NDHS dataset does not contain codes for the states - only names. Therefore we need to join the two data frames using the name of the state - and checking that all states have data.

Show the code 
vect_state_geo_NDHS <- dplyr::left_join(vect_state_geo, df_NDHS_state, by = c("adm1_ref_name"  = "State"))
vect_state_geo_NDHS |> as.data.frame() |> 
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = F,
    filter = "bottom",
    selection = list(mode = "none"),
    editable = FALSE,
    options = list(
      digits = 0,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      scrollCollapse = TRUE,
      autoWidth = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = list(leftColumns = 2),
      lengthMenu = c(15, 40),
      pageLength = 15
    ))

Join the NDHS database to the zone dataset

The NDHS dataset does not contain codes for the zones - only names. Therefore we need to join the two data frames using the name of the zone - and checking that all zones have data.

Show the code 
vect_zone_gpz_NDHS <- dplyr::left_join(vect_gpz_geo, df_NDHS_zone, by = c("geopolitical_zone"  = "Zone"))
vect_zone_gpz_NDHS |> as.data.frame() |> 
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = F,
    filter = "bottom",
    selection = list(mode = "none"),
    editable = FALSE,
    options = list(
      digits = 0,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      scrollCollapse = TRUE,
      autoWidth = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = list(leftColumns = 2),
      lengthMenu = c(15, 40),
      pageLength = 15
    ))

Modelled Data from 2018/19 Food consumption

It was decided not to use the data from this study, for two reasons. Firstly the data are now quite old and the other sources are more recent. Secondly, the deficiency values are imputed from dietary intake rather than from biomarkers.

Compare data sources

To help select the best data source it is necessary to compare the statistics for each indicator from the two sources.

Vitamin A deficiency

Vitamin A deficiency is only available from the NFCMS data, and therefore there is no spatial variation below the geopolitical zone level.

There are data for women of reproductive age and children between 6 and 59 months.

Vitamin A deficiency in women of reproductive age (NFCMS, 2021)

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_def_vit_A_pc_246)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = WRA_def_vit_A_pc_246), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in women of reproductive age", fill = " %") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The highest values for vitamin A deficiency among women are in North West zone with 22.2%. These values are almost double the next highest value in South South. The lowest values are in South East with 3.4% of women with a deficiency.

Vitamin A deficiency in children (NFCMS, 2021)

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_def_vit_A_pc_236)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_def_vit_A_pc_236), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in children", fill = " %") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The pattern of vitamin A deficiency among children is similar, with the highest value again in North West zone with 50.6%. These values are 20% greater than in North East - the zone with next highest value. The lowest values were again in South East with 6.1% of children with a vitamin A deficiency.

Iron deficiency

Iron deficiency in women of reproductive age (NFCMS, 2021)

Iron deficiency is defined as serum ferritin concentration <15 µg/L corrected for inflammation.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_def_iron_pc_245)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = WRA_def_iron_pc_245), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of iron deficiency in women of reproductive age", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

Iron deficiency in women of reproductive age is highest in North East geopolitical zone, followed by South South and South East - all three had values higher than 10%. The zone with lowest value was South West.

Anaemia in women of reproductive age (NFCMS, 2021)

Iron deficiency anaemia defined as serum ferritin concentration <15 µg/L, adjusted for inflammation and adjusted haemoglobin <12 g/dL Estimates calculated using weights that account for survey design and non-response.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_def_anaemia_pc_245)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = WRA_def_anaemia_pc_245), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of anaemia in women of reproductive age", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The variation among zones of iron deficiency anaemia was small, varying between 4.7% and 5.5%, except in South West where the percentage of anaemic women was only 1.6%. The North East zone once again had the highest rate.

Anaemia in women of reproductive age (NDHS, 2023-24)

The Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey of 2023-24 gives data for four levels of anaemia: (1) Any; (2) Mild; (3) Moderate, and; (4) Severe anaemia.

Any anaemia is when haemoglobin level <12.0 g/dl

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_zone_gpz_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_anaemia_any)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = WRA_anaemia_any), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of anaemia (any) in women of reproductive age", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The zone with the highest percentage of women with anaemia was South East, with over 50% of women. The other zones all had values between 40% and 50%. The zone with the lowest levels was North Central.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_state_geo_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_anaemia_any)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = WRA_anaemia_any), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of anaemia (any) in women of reproductive age", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The individual states show a more mixed pattern. The state with the highest value is Ebonyi with 71.8% of women anaemic. Other states in the same zone (South East) have lower values, such as Imo with 41.7%.

In North West zone there are instances of negative spatial auto-correlation where neighbouring states have very different values - a clear example is the difference between Sokoto (67.7%) and Kebbi (21.4%). States in South West zone, in contrast, have more similar values.

The zone with the highest percentage of women with mild anaemia was South East, with over 30% of women. The other zones all had values between 20% and 30%. The zone with the lowest levels was North West

Show the code

Compare sources

The only micro nutrient for which there are data in different sources is for iron. However, there are some differences in the indicators used for iron deficiency anaemia in the two sources.

The NDHS has a finer spatial resolution, and the data were collected more recently. The only issue would be to decide which of the four anaemia indicators to use.

Iron deficiency in children between 6 and 59 months (NFCMS, 2021)

Iron deficiency is defined as serum ferritin concentration <15 µg/L corrected for inflammation.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_gpz_geo_NFCMS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_def_iron_pc_235)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_def_iron_pc_235), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of iron deficiency in children between 6 and 59 months", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

Iron deficiency among children in 2021 was far higher in the northern geopolitical zones than in the south. North East zone had the highest values while South South had the lowest. This was a differing pattern to that for women of reproductive age.

Anaemia in children between 6 and 59 months (NDHS, 2023-24)

The Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey of 2023-24 gives data for four levels of anaemia: (1) Any; (2) Mild; (3) Moderate, and; (4) Severe anaemia.

Any anaemia is when haemoglobin level <12.0 g/dl

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_zone_gpz_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_anaemia_any)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_anaemia_any), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of anaemia (any) in children between 6 and 59 months", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

Levels of child anaemia are high throughout Nigeria with five out of six zones showing rates above 50%. The zone with the highest percentage is South East with 63.7%, while the lowest is in South West with 45.5%.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_state_geo_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_anaemia_any)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_anaemia_any), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",

  theme(

    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The individual states show a more mixed pattern. The state with the highest value is Ebonyi with 84.8% of children anaemic, the next highest value is 74.5% in Akwa Ibom state in South South zone.

The state with the lowest value is Delta state with 33.4%.

Mild anaemia when haemoglobin level 11.0–11.9 g/dl

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_zone_gpz_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_anaemia_mild)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_anaemia_mild), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of anaemia (mild) in children between 6 and 59 months", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

The zone with the highest percentage of women with mild anaemia was South South, with over 30% of children However all zones had values between 26% and 32%. The zone with the lowest levels was South West.

There are some very big differences in the levels of moderate anaemia among the states - with a low of 9% in the Federal Capital Territory and Delta states, while both Akwa Ibom and Zamfara had levels above 40%.

These are patterns which were masked in the zone map.

Severe anaemia when haemoglobin level <8.0 g/dl

  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),

  )

There was a different spatial pattern for severe anaemia. The zone with the highest percentage of children with severe anaemia was North East, 2.5% of children anaemic. The other zones varied between 0.1% and 1.8%. The zone with the lowest levels was South West. This showed a similar pattern to the values for women of reproductive age.

Show the code 
ggplot(vect_state_geo_NDHS) +
  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = CH_anaemia_sev)) +
  geom_spatvector_text(aes(label = CH_anaemia_sev), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,

    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

Levels of severe anaemia show less obvious differences within geopolitical zones, except in North East where Adamawa has the highest value for any state with 4.6% but neighbouring Borno has a value of 0.8%. North West zone also has large differences among states, while states in South West zone have consistently low vales for severe anaemia.

Compare sources

The only micro nutrient for which there are data in different sources is for iron. However, there are some differences in the indicators used for iron deficiency anaemia in the two sources.

The NDHS has a finer spatial resolution, and the data were collected more recently. The only issue would be to decide which of the four anaemia indicators to use.

Zinc deficiency

Zinc deficiency in women of reproductive age (NFCMS, 2021)

Show the code

  geom_spatvector(aes(fill = WRA_def_zinc_pc_252)) +

  scale_fill_stepsn(
    n.breaks = 10,
    limits = c(0, 100),
    colours = hcl.colors(palette = "Grays", 10, rev = T),
    guide = "legend",
    na.value = "pink",
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(title = "Prevalence of zinc deficiency in women of reproductive age", fill = "%") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(),
    legend.title = element_markdown(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

There are large differences in the percentage of women of reproductive age with zinc deficiency among geopolitical zones in Nigeria. The zone with the lowest values is South East, with 15.5%, whereas in North West over 60% of women are deficient in zinc.
